This is a concept drift violation (RC-04) and hallucination violation (RC-05). The corrected question compares TDMA with FDMA, both of which are defined in Module 3, using parameters (bandwidth utilization, synchronization requirements) that are explicitly covered in the academic content.

input.academic_content: Time Division Multiple Access (TDMA) divides the channel by time. Frequency Division Multiple Access (FDMA) divides the channel by frequency. TDMA requires strict synchronization. FDMA requires guard bands between frequency slots. TDMA has higher bandwidth efficiency when traffic is bursty. FDMA is simpler to implement but wastes bandwidth when users are idle.
input.expected_answer: TDMA vs FDMA comparison: TDMA divides time, FDMA divides frequency. TDMA needs synchronization, FDMA needs guard bands. TDMA is bandwidth efficient for bursty traffic. FDMA is simpler. Tabular comparison preferred.
